searchText: I think delaying the bomb for 700,000 blocks is very good idea. But, I also think it might benefit the group to "soft target" a mid- to late-August date for the Merge (but not mention that in the EIP). Why not give yourselves some breathing room? Also, just thinking out loud -- is it necessary that 100% of the EL-CL pairs merges successfully? (I'm speaking out of ignorance here.) Would 90% of the pairs merging correctly with the Sepolia and Goerli testnets be a success? Ropsten merged but not all pairs worked. It was still a successful merge, right? Perhaps you could define success for the first test merge at 90% and the second at 95%... ~everyone going to run geth anyway... Well, primary concern is securing the network with client diversity right? The other way around, major CEX like Binance has a large ETH2 staking pool, and they can have incentive to do short-term mining for smooth transitions. Pure PoW miners do not like PoS, but they are the minorities in governance and the best they can do is to maintain a PoW fork and hope for the best <@478178670637219840> suggested we > ... plan with transaction replay protection in mind (because both the PoS chain and PoW chain may survive) I guess I just wanted reassurance on that. I don't think there is a necessity in 100% nodes running through the merge transition without any issue. I pretty much agree with Danny's summary here https://twitter.com/dannyryan/status/1534928769005170688 I guess this wouldn't have resulted in big penalties for those 9% of operators? I think we should aim for 99% though, for the transition to be considered smooth I think if ropsten repeated on mainnet it would be completely fine 100% agree with this. "Zeroism" of bugs or perfectionism *in the newer EL clients* + using this to artificially slow down the merge dates doesn't help anybody IMO; Correct me if I'm wrong, but given that the current minority EL clients *remain* minority at the time of the merge (highly likely simply because they are 'new'), bugs specific to them wouldn't cause slashings for the users of these new clients, and such users can easily switch to another client in case of bugs, then go back once the bug is solved. Over time, as the newer EL clients gain more market share (as they mature and get battle-tested), then they naturally become more critical in sense of "being free of bugs" - but today IMO their value add is really the extra optionality for stakers. This might be controversial, but IMO Ropsten proved the network as a whole is ready to go, and we should skip having Goerli + Sepolia as a "pre-requisite" to go mainnet as its causing a lot of extra work with little added value (e.g., instead of new ELs spending time fixing the last issues, time needs to be devoted coordinating all the testnet transitions). The whole point of having multiple clients is that its okay and expected to have a few issues, *especially* in the case of a minority client.. I think preparations to sepolia are too advanced to skip it and a good last rehearsal, but the value of merge on goerli is questionable, yes. why not merge mainnet in late july instead, assuming sepolia goes well. Makes sense, as a middle ground Goerli is planned to be done with 'Final' version of clients and as final dress rehearsal before mainnet. Sepolia as I understand won't have the final version. Client teams will only progress to Goerli when they are satisfied with their own clients passing all tests iirc Unfortunately not waiting for minority clients would result into further worsening of client diversity due to stickyness of clients once set up IMO. The best thing the community can hope is a faster mainnet release candidate and a smoother Goerli merge. You know it is not a *yet* another simple hardfork like London. It's a structural change in the Ethereum protocol and it will take a month or two for people to just sync a beacon node and configure two nodes to work together <@354681205842771973> And in general, sorry, I don't think that "Why not" approach is appropriate for a platform that holds ~~a trillion~~ $125B of user funds. IMHO when you have only one attempt, and there is $125B of **user funds** locked in your platform, there should be ZERO bugs. Also - if this upgrade fails, do note that hard fork coordinators and people who pressed the "Release" button on GitHub on a release that enabled the hf will be legally responsible for all losses. No one would take this risk. > that enabled the hf will be legally responsible for all losses. No one would take this risk. Lol no. And please stop discussing this random stuff in <#745077610685661265> It's not random stuff It's on topic Spouting falsehoods is always off-topic Let's move to <#595721451651465227> It's related to infrastructural node operators, not to the stakers. So, no penalties at all Sepolia and Goerly are prerequisites, we're aiming to run the Mainnet upgrade with near the same client versions as we will have on Goerly (as <@140789012276183040> has commented) hmm but if a staker is connected to one, they are unable to vote if they are out of sync? Oh, yes. I have messed this a bit. It was related to nodes running nimbus team validators, yes, these validators have experienced penalties but considering that the issue has been resolved quickly and the network was healthy the size of the penalties should have been marginal hmm, but 9% of the network being offline would result quite significant penalties. But I guess on mainnet this would not have lasted for long FYI, we've released Geth 1.10.19 shipping the Gray Glacier difficulty bomb hard fork https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/releases/tag/v1.10.19 9% of the network offline would result in a reduction in rewards of the active validators of 9% (i.e. down to 91% of maximum, assuming they are validating correctly). The validators that were offline would suffer standard non-attestation (and non-sync committee) penalties Do we still want to have all clients pass hive tests? Because that looks as if it will take awhile: https://hivetests2.ethdevops.io/ I am neither involved enough or knowledgeable enough to say anything on that matter 🙂 IMO, all clients passing merge tests on hive is one of prerequisites. Client teams and test engineers (as tests may also be broken) are working on it lolz: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey_Glacier https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray_Glacier I din't expect to need to be glacier expert haha this was mentioned in the naming conversation that this could be confusing... <:troll:688452927005786222> If we have to push the bomb back again, let's not call it "Grey Glacier". To add to this: the newer EL clients that are repeatedly failing testnets have *single digit* adoption. Geth has 80% adoption (https://ethernodes.org/). Wtf is the point in delaying the merge - a consensus layer change - to wait for EL teams that have 5-8% adoption?! ^ IMO the best counter argument to this is that every bug fixed in _any_ client is _potentially_ a bug that exists in _every_ client. Also sometimes the majority client has a bug that's not found until a minority client implements the same functionality and gets different results. The Merge is also the best opportunity we'll have to make progress on EL client diversity given it requires all stakers to run one. If we have a majority client on the EL, the same risks exists as on the CL, where a bug could lead to the wrong chain being finalized and be very painful to unwind. If we can get geth below 2/3rd of validator nodes at the merge, that's very valuable. Good explainer here: https://dankradfeist.de/ethereum/2022/03/24/run-the-majority-client-at-your-own-peril.html I still don't know which one is it With all due respect, these are two different objectives. 1. Trying to improve EL client diversity (via measures implemented at the protocol layer or social layer) 2. Switching the underlying consensus mechanism of a 200bil network. Trying to do both is like trying to make a sandwhich while showering. Basic project management suggests they should be tackled serially, not concurrently Gr**a**y, the one that merges with another glacier, not Gr**e**y I disagree they are separate: we have multiple EL clients today. It's not like we are building them from scratch. If one implementation was several months behind another, sure, it doesn't make sense to wait for them forever. That said, assuming they are all ready relatively around the same time, then I don't see why we should do things any differently than for every other network upgrade, especially given this is a case where we can expect the needle to move significantly more. <@751712784852451359> re-reading your previous comment, I just want to make sure you understand that the merge requires changes on both the EL and CL clients. It's not just a change on the CL side. but the majority of change from EL perspective is in consensus and its interfaces right? (not sync, EVM, EL storage, etc) Nethermind 1.13.3 with difficulty bomb delay: https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/releases/tag/1.13.3 The thing is IMHO no implementation is yet ready, some are closer than others but still 🤷‍♂️
